swap.evidence: Swapped products: a council parking-permit application and a GP practice appointment booker. Elements that survive unchanged: white header bar + wordmark, pale grey-blue ground, single left column of ~320px native inputs, dark-teal rectangular primary button, pink-bordered 'There is a problem' summary, bordered radio cards, key/value summary list, white footer with a phone number. Elements bound to this product: the copy (sill gate, HW, draught, pontoon, 'Settles on soft mud at low water'), the anchor glyph, and the tide table's content. With name and copy hidden a reader could not tell this is for boats or a tidal harbour.

category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a small public/municipal booking service: one-column public-service form pattern with native controls, a dark accent button, a bordered error summary and a summary list, light ground, system-like humanist sans. Predicted opposite: a glossy nautical marketing look (navy/white stripes, wave graphics, hero photo of yachts). Every identity-carrying element matches the default: ground, type voice, colour anchor (dark teal), components and layout.

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'online pitch booking for a small coastal campsite; visitors pick dates, a pitch that fits their van, give vehicle details, pay on arrival'. Predicted choices: same single-column form, same radio cards ('Pitch 6, vans up to 8 metres, £x per night'), same summary list and confirmation sentence, same calm dark accent. Overlap is essentially total; nothing in the render was driven by the tide/sill-gate mechanism that the brief names as the differentiator.

mode_fit.judgement: conventional structure is correct for these Operate/Read surfaces; no hero moments, no motion seen, standard controls and navigation. The gap is the identity floor (name as a designed mark, ground, type and colour from the harbour's world, and one signature from the tide/gate mechanism), which Operate surfaces still need; that gap is not a mode violation.

findings.title: No signature from the tide and sill-gate mechanism anywhere in the journey
findings.description: The brief names the tide as what sets this harbour apart (arrival only in the sill-gate window around high water). In the render this appears only as prose and as a default 7-row table on /; the arrival-time select, the berth cards and the review never show the gate window or the tide visually. The rest of the frame (ground, type, components) is the category default, so the swap, category-guess and similar-prompt tests all fail.
findings.impact: With nothing of its own, the service may read to a new visiting skipper as any council form, and the one thing they most need to plan around (the gate window) has no visual presence where they choose the arrival time.
findings.recommendation: Decide (and record in DESIGN.md) one signature drawn from the gate/tide mechanism that recurs quietly where arrival time is chosen and confirmed, within Operate-mode limits.

findings.title: Identity floor missing: name set as body text on an unchosen pale ground
findings.description: The only identity is an anchor glyph and 'Saltmarsh Quay' in bold body-size type. Ground, type and accent are not traceable to the harbour's world, and with DESIGN.md missing nothing records why they were chosen. Every screen is heading, controls, button; none has a focal point.
findings.impact: The pages are likely to read as plain and template-like to visitors, which may lower confidence that this small harbour's booking is cared for.
findings.recommendation: Write DESIGN.md attributes from the harbour's world, then decide the name's treatment, ground and accent from them so the identity is present on every Operate screen without adding hero moments.

findings.title: Tide table column headers misaligned with right-aligned time figures
findings.description: 'Morning' and 'Afternoon' headers are left-aligned at the start of their columns while the HW times are right-aligned at the far edge, so at 1280 'Morning' sits ~80px left of its figures and 'Afternoon' appears closer to the morning times.
findings.impact: Skippers reading HW times quickly may pair a header with the wrong column; the only product-bound element looks unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Align numeric column headers with their figures.

findings.title: Tide times shown in UTC while arrival times and the brief use local time
findings.description: The table caption says 'times in UTC'; the arrival time chosen and echoed on /berths.html and /review.html (15:00) is local, and context.md specifies 24-hour local times. On 17 October local time is UTC+1, so the gate window cannot be read off the table against the arrival time without mental arithmetic.
findings.impact: A skipper may pick an arrival time an hour off the gate window, which is the one planning error the harbour cares about.

evidence.detail: 'High water at the quay, times in UTC'

findings.recommendation: Decide one time basis for the whole journey, matching the brief's local-time format.

findings.title: Overflow '...' button floats detached from the content and its menu shifts the berth list
findings.description: On /berths.html the '...' button sits alone at the far right (x≈1030-1072) in a ~70px empty band, outside the 752px card column; opening it inserts the menu into flow and pushes the whole berth list down ~115px rather than overlaying. 'Change dates', a core task, is hidden behind it.
findings.impact: The isolated control draws an early fixation away from the berth choice, the layout jump may disorient on a phone held one-handed, and a core task is less discoverable.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether these actions need an overflow at all; if kept, anchor them to the content column and stop the menu from reflowing the list.

findings.title: Invalid fields inconsistently marked in error states
findings.description: In each error state one invalid field keeps the normal dark border while its siblings turn red: Length on /boat.html errors, the Arrival time select on / errors, Skipper's name on /review.html errors. All have an error message above them.
findings.impact: A skipper scanning for which fields to fix may skip the unmarked one; the state looks unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Apply the invalid treatment to every field that has an error message.

findings.title: Footer stops short, leaving an empty band of page ground below it on short pages
findings.description: On /boat.html, /review.html and /confirmed.html at 1280x900, and the booking-stopped state at 375, the white footer ends mid-viewport and the pale page ground continues beneath it (up to ~500px on the stopped screen).
findings.impact: Reads as an unfinished layout; on the confirmation and stopped screens the page looks half-loaded.
findings.recommendation: Decide how short pages end so the footer and ground meet the viewport bottom.

findings.title: Booking reference not given prominence on confirmation; arrival time omitted
findings.description: On /confirmed.html the reference SQ-1017-C3, which the copy says to keep to hand, is a bold fragment inside a body sentence, no more prominent than the summary rows. The summary lists Arrival as a date only; the 15:00 arrival time, the tide-critical fact, is dropped.
findings.impact: A skipper glancing back at the screen on board may not find the reference or the time they committed to quickly.
findings.recommendation: Decide the confirmation's focal point (the reference) and include the arrival time with the date.

findings.title: Browser-default date control shows yyyy/mm/dd on an en-GB service
findings.description: The Arrival date field is an unthemed native date input whose placeholder reads 'yyyy/mm/dd' at every width, while the product formats dates as 'Saturday 17 October 2026'.
findings.impact: The first control a visitor meets looks default and uses an unfamiliar order, which may cause day/month errors.
findings.recommendation: Decide a date entry pattern that matches the en-GB format.

findings.title: Summary list keeps a wide label column at 320, wrapping values to three lines
findings.description: On /review.html at 320 the label column keeps ~150px, so 'Saturday 17 October 2026 at 15:00' wraps to three lines and 'Curlew, 10.4 metres long' and '£74.88, paid on arrival' strand single words. Detector TYP-15 (#s-arrival, #s-total) corroborates.
findings.impact: At large text sizes, common among older skippers, the booking summary becomes a ragged column that is harder to check before confirming.
findings.recommendation: Decide how the summary list reflows at narrow widths.

findings.title: Stranded words and split reference at narrow widths
findings.description: Reference 'BK-' / '409.' splits across lines on the booking-stopped screen at 375; H1s strand 'space' (/berths.html 320/375) and 'booking' (/review.html 375). Detector TYP-15 corroborates.
findings.impact: A split reference may be misread or mis-quoted to the harbour office; stranded headline words make narrow views look unfinished.

evidence.detail: TYP-15 hits on #dead-end > p and #main > h1

findings.recommendation: Keep references unbreakable and balance headline wraps.

strengths: Copy in the skippers' own words, matter-of-fact and specific (sill gate, HW, draught hint, 'Settles on soft mud at low water', 'Nothing is charged online').
High text contrast and large tap targets suit bright-light, one-handed use.
One clear primary action per screen and a consistent linked error summary.
keep: Keep the plain, specific copy and the single-primary-action structure; add identity and the tide signature around them, not instead of them.
notes: No baseline/ in the packet, so pairwise is not applicable. DESIGN.md is missing, so brand fit (DES-04) is not assessable and DEC-02 is not met; the brand_fit rubric score is effectively n/a. Verdict file written before unsealing; no source, builder notes or other critics' outputs were read. Forced-colours, more-contrast and CVD variants were not reviewed in detail.
